questions.question: What does weather describe?
choices: The motion of Earth's tectonic plates
Average conditions over many decades
Atmospheric conditions at a particular time and place
Only the amount of annual rainfall

questions.question: Which reservoir contains most of Earth's water?
choices: Atmospheric clouds
Oceans
Rivers
Lakes

questions.question: Which term describes the temperature at which cooling air reaches water-vapor saturation?
choices: Heat index
Wind chill
Daily maximum temperature
Dew point

questions.question: Which process releases water vapor from plants?
choices: Infiltration
Runoff
Precipitation
Transpiration

questions.question: What is precipitation?
choices: Water falling from clouds as rain, snow, or other forms
Water soaking into the ground
Water vapor moving through a leaf
Liquid water changing into gas

questions.question: Which instrument measures atmospheric pressure?
choices: Rain gauge
Barometer
Anemometer
Thermometer

questions.question: What is infiltration?
choices: Water vapor turning into droplets
Water flowing across the ground
Water entering the soil from the surface
Cloud droplets forming ice crystals

questions.question: What supplies much of the energy that drives evaporation in the water cycle?
choices: Ocean tides
The Sun
Rock formation
Earth's magnetic field

questions.question: How does gravity contribute to the water cycle?
choices: It prevents water from entering rivers
It converts water vapor directly into heat
It makes all groundwater rise to the surface
It moves falling precipitation and downhill-flowing water

questions.question: What are most clouds made of?
choices: Tiny liquid droplets or ice crystals
Visible water vapor gas alone
Only dry air under high pressure
Large raindrops resting without air movement

questions.question: Why can cooling moist air lead to cloud formation?
choices: Cooling adds new water molecules to otherwise dry air
Cooling always increases the air's capacity to hold water vapor
Cooling can bring air to saturation, allowing condensation
Cooling guarantees precipitation before droplets form

questions.question: What generally causes wind?
choices: Differences in cloud color alone
Equal atmospheric pressure at every location
Changes in ocean salinity alone
Differences in atmospheric pressure

questions.question: Why can replacing soil with pavement increase storm runoff?
choices: Pavement makes rain fall faster
Less water can soak into the ground
Pavement eliminates gravity
More water is stored inside plant roots

questions.question: Why can mountains cause wetter conditions on one side?
choices: Air descending a mountain always cools
Mountains create water from rock
Rising moist air cools and can produce precipitation
Rain can fall only above high elevations

questions.question: How are weather and climate related?
choices: Climate summarizes patterns of weather over long periods
Climate refers only to a single day's temperature
They describe exactly the same time scale
Weather is a measure of climate in one instant only

questions.question: A wet sidewalk dries on a sunny day. Which process chiefly removes its liquid water?
choices: Condensation
Infiltration into clouds
Evaporation
Freezing

questions.question: A forecast gives a 40% chance of rain for a location and period. What does this express?
choices: A prediction that rainfall will be 40 millimeters
A guarantee that rain will last 40% of the day
A claim that 40% of every raindrop will evaporate
A probability of measurable precipitation

questions.question: Two nearby fields receive equal rain. One is vegetated; the other has compacted bare soil. Which outcome is more likely?
choices: The compacted field has more runoff and erosion
Both must have identical runoff
The vegetated field cannot absorb water
The bare field produces no runoff

questions.question: Water evaporates from an ocean, condenses, and falls on land. What does this sequence demonstrate?
choices: Water is permanently used up during evaporation
Water moves between Earth's connected reservoirs
Only fresh water can evaporate
Clouds are separate from the water cycle

questions.question: A student compares rainfall at two locations. Which method provides the fairest comparison?
choices: Use comparable rain gauges over the same time period
Place one gauge under a roof
Record only the wetter days at each site
Use different collection periods at each site
